items.headline: Researchers warn use of AI in writing could 'homogenise human writing and thought'
items.excerpt: New research warns that widespread adoption of AI language models in writing could flatten stylistic diversity and individual perspective. Academics say the risk is not just to prose style but to the range of thought writers bring to the page.

items.headline: AI debate has shifted from 'can we to should we', IPG Autumn Conference 2026 hears
items.excerpt: The Independent Publishers Guild's autumn conference put AI at the centre of its programme, with new research finding that 'AI may have damaged trust more than it has changed workflows.' Speakers argued the industry question has moved from technical feasibility to editorial ethics.

items.headline: Letting ChatGPT write your emails has a bigger impact than you think
items.excerpt: Author Daisy Buchanan argues that handing even routine correspondence to AI erodes a skill writers depend on: 'Outsourcing writing to AI - yes, even the boring bits - robs us of a life-enhancing skill.'

items.headline: Publishing's AI Reckoning
items.excerpt: Four years after ChatGPT's release, publishers report AI has mostly landed in back-office work - metadata, royalty statements, admin - while firm lines hold around core creative work like title selection and cover design. The piece maps where the industry has actually settled.

items.headline: PW Spotlight: Time to Reclaim the Driver's Seat in AI
items.excerpt: Bookpact.ai, founded by Sander Ruys, is a licensing platform that lets publishers set per-deal terms, compensation and usage tracking for how AI companies access their titles. (Marked Sponsored / PW Studio content.)

items.headline: The Cost of Deepfakes: PW Talks with Meena Kandasamy
items.excerpt: In the novelist's 'Fieldwork as a Sex Object' (Soft Skull, Nov.), a young Indian woman faces harassment after someone posts a deepfake video of her. Kandasamy discusses writing fiction about synthetic media harm.

items.headline: Who is Narrating the Future? AI and the Audiobook Market
items.excerpt: A Frankfurter Buchmesse / Dosdoce.com white paper finds 85% of audio professionals now use AI somewhere in production, but only 17% have integrated it across more than six production phases. Listener willingness to try AI-narrated titles fell from 70% in 2025 to 61% in 2026.

items.headline: Find Your Memoir Voice Before AI Flattens It
items.excerpt: A craft piece on protecting authorial voice from AI-smoothed prose: a standout voice is a mixture of natural style and sentence-level decisions that bring who you are to life. Practical drills for memoirists working alongside AI drafting tools.

items.headline: Get ready for AI agents to come knocking on your door
items.excerpt: A new app called iLands allows the creation of autonomous AI agents that not only write articles but pitch their work to media outlets. Editors and agents are about to face inbound submissions from software, not people.

items.headline: Ask the Chefs: AI and Copyright Licensing
items.excerpt: The US Department of Justice filed a Statement of Interest in the NYT v. OpenAI/Microsoft copyright litigation, largely siding with the AI companies and favoring LLM training as fair use. A panel of publishing experts reacts to what it means for content licensing.

items.headline: Guest Post - The Unbundling of Scholarly Publishing: A Trilemma for the AI Era
items.excerpt: The journal portfolio, platform, or membership is no longer enough as AI transforms how research is discovered and consumed. The authors lay out three competing strategies publishers must choose between.

items.headline: What Machines Can't Replace: Why AI Makes Us More Human With Anna McPhee
items.excerpt: Author and creative technologist Anna McPhee describes using AI for research, editing, admin and marketing while still writing every word herself. The interview is a working model for where indie authors draw the line.

items.headline: The Evolving World of Literary Rights: Moving Beyond the Printed Page
items.excerpt: An essay on how literary rights have stretched from print to screens, games and now AI systems, and what that means for how authors and agents negotiate deals today.

items.headline: Simon & Schuster is making indie publishing easier
items.excerpt: Simon & Schuster's new indie imprints let self-publishing authors attach a major publisher's logo to their books - positioned partly as a credibility signal that helps titles stand out from the flood of AI-generated output.

items.headline: Flowtica Verso is an e-Ink AI screen that attaches to your phone
items.excerpt: The Flowtica Verso's always-on e-paper display sets it apart from standard screenless AI voice recorders, pairing ambient AI capture with an E-Ink reading surface.

items.headline: AI Updates, Remembering Dolly Parton, and More News for Library Workers
items.excerpt: Book Riot's library roundup leads with AI developments hitting library workflows - vendor tools, patron-facing chatbots and collection policy - alongside a tribute to Dolly Parton's literacy work.
